subject: Cross-border DPA: signoff playbook and SCCs fallback path
messages:
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@datamed.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@datamed.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DataMed DPA redlines + SCCs fallback proposal

Hi Rishi / Ben,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Attached is DataMed's clean redline of the DPA (see DataMed_DPA_Redlines_20260527.docx) — high level changes are:
- Narrower subprocessors list clause (we added a 30-day notice to customers rather than immediate consent).
- A proposed export carveout for analytics processing that routes logs through our EU-only pipeline.
- New language on SCCs fallback that lists a manual review path if adequacy decisions change.

Two asks from our side:
1) Can Redwood confirm whether the SCCs fallback wording is operationally acceptable (we tried to keep it process-oriented rather than prescriptive)?
2) We'll need an ETA for evidence (KMS architecture diagram + hosting regions) for our procurement team — procurement@datamed.com is copied.

We're hoping to move the redline to signature next week; happy to jump on a quick 20-min call if helpful.

Best,
Sarah Nguyen
Head of Legal Ops | DataMed
[sarah@datamed.com]

Attachment: DataMed_DPA_Redlines_20260527.docx
Attachment: SCCs-Fallback-Diagram.png

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@datamed.com>, procurement@datamed.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DataMed DPA redlines + SCCs fallback proposal

Thanks Sarah — received and reviewed quickly. Forwarding internally to map changes to our signoff checklist. High-level notes:

- SCCs fallback: the proposed process-oriented language looks OK, but ops will need a clear escalation SLA (we should avoid open-ended "manual review").
- Export carveout for analytics: this is fine if we can pin processing to our EU-hosted private cluster and provide the KMS diagram requested.
- Subprocessor notice: 30-day notice is standard. Legal may want to keep a narrow exception for security-critical subprocessors.

Internal asks for Ben/Laura:
1) Ben — can you confirm with infra whether we can produce the KMS/hosting diagram and a short operations note that maps to the SCCs fallback steps by EOD Monday? If we can provide that, DataMed's procurement team will likely move fast.
2) Laura — please review the redlines and call out anything non-negotiable (liability / indemnity / data residency). I flagged the fallback SLA item for your attention.

I'll propose a 25-min sync Monday with DataMed if both internal items look doable.

--

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Sarah Nguyen <sarah@datamed.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2026 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DataMed DPA redlines + SCCs fallback proposal

Rishi / Laura / Sarah — quick infra update after sprint with ops:

- KMS + hosting diagram: ops team can produce a sanitized diagram (no private IPs) showing EU-only keys and the private cluster by COB Monday (2026-06-01). We'll include which subnets are EU-only and the key rotation cadence.
- SCCs fallback SLA: ops suggests a 72-hour acknowledgement and 10-business-day remediation window for any fallback execution. That gives legal time to triage and customers some predictability.
- Analytics carveout: confirmed we can pin processing to the EU cluster for the DataMed deal. We will document the routing in the evidence package.

Laura, flagged items for legal negotiation:
- We should accept the 30-day subprocessor notice but request an exception for emergency security patches so we can onboard critical monitoring services within 48 hours.
- The liability cap and indemnity language in DataMed redline reduces our liability in a way we can't accept — I recommend counter-proposing to keep our standard cap and add a limited carveout for GDPR-regulated processing only.

Action items:
- Ops to deliver evidence package (KMS diagram + hosting regions + routing note) by 2026-06-01.
- Legal (Laura) to send counter-proposed liability paragraph and the emergency subprocessor exception language by EOD Tue.

If both are ready, Rishi — you can schedule the signoff call with DataMed for 2026-06-02.

--
Ben Carter
Director, Contracts & Privacy | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
Attachment: SCCs-Fallback-Diagram.png

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Sarah Nguyen <sarah@datamed.com>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2026 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DataMed DPA redlines + SCCs fallback proposal

Thanks all — I reviewed DataMed's redlines and Ben's infra notes. Summary / legal position:

1) SCCs fallback SLA: Acceptable if we convert "manual review" into a defined two-step process: 72-hour acknowledgement + technical remediation window of up to 10 business days. Include an internal on-call escalation path (we'll add a contact stub in the evidence pack).
2) Subprocessor notice: Accept 30-day notice; counter-propose emergency onboarding exception (48h) for security-critical services; include a short list of staff roles that can approve this (Security Director + Head of Infra).
3) Liability / indemnity: Do not accept DataMed's reduced cap as-is. I will propose language to preserve Redwood's standard cap with a narrow carveout for regulatory fines to be split per standard market practice.

Next steps:
- Ben to upload the evidence package to the Drive folder and post the link (ops said 2026-06-01).
- I will draft a short redline (two paragraphs) for the liability carveout and emergency subprocessor language by Tue EOD 2026-06-01.
- Rishi to confirm 2026-06-02 signoff call at 0900 BST if procurement is ready.

Sarah — thanks for keeping the SCCs language operational rather than prescriptive; that made negotiation straightforward. If DataMed can accept the SLA + emergency exception, we should be able to move to DocuSign the same week.
